title: Digital SAT Suite

exam.scoring: 400-1600 scale (R&W 54 Q/64 min; Math 44 Q/70 min)

content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the College Board digital SAT description: Reading & Writing and Math modules to the published domain weightings. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: A city planted rows of trees along its hottest streets. During summer, air temperatures on those blocks fell by several degrees, while unplanted blocks nearby stayed hot. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Planting trees can lower air temperatures on urban streets.
Trees are expensive for cities to maintain over time.
Summer temperatures vary from block to block for unknown reasons.
Unplanted streets attract more traffic than tree-lined ones do.
items.explanation: The text connects tree planting with lower summer air temperatures on those streets; it does not discuss cost, traffic, or unknown causes.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Information and Ideas

items.stem: In a study of memory, participants who slept after learning a list of words recalled more words the next day than participants who stayed awake. According to the text, which group recalled more words?
options: Only participants who studied the list twice recalled more.
Participants who slept after learning the list
Participants who stayed awake all night
Both groups recalled the same number of words.
items.explanation: The text states that those who slept after learning recalled more words; the awake group recalled fewer, and no other group is mentioned.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Information and Ideas

items.stem: A biologist observed that frogs in a pond containing fish were active only at night, whereas frogs in a nearby fishless pond were active both day and night. Which choice is the most reasonable inference?
options: Fish consume the plants that the frogs require.
The fishless pond is always warmer than the other pond.
The frogs' daytime activity is likely limited by the risk of fish predation.
Frogs are unable to swim when fish are present.
items.explanation: Night-only activity where fish are present suggests the frogs avoid fish during the day; the text supports no other explanation.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Information and Ideas

items.stem: A researcher claims that a certain plant produces a chemical that deters insects. Which finding would most directly support this claim?
options: The plant grows taller than other plants nearby.
The chemical is colorless and odorless.
The plant produces flowers in early spring.
Insects avoided leaves that had been coated with the chemical.
items.explanation: If insects avoid leaves treated with the chemical, that directly supports the claim that the chemical deters them; the other findings are unrelated.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Information and Ideas

items.stem: A student records the number of bee visits to two flower colors over one hour. Red flowers received 40 visits, and yellow flowers received 10. Which choice best describes the data?
options: Bees visited the red flowers about four times as often as the yellow ones.
Bees visited the yellow flowers more often than the red ones.
The two colors received an equal number of visits.
Bees visited neither color during the hour.
items.explanation: Since 40 is four times 10, bees visited the red flowers about four times as often; the other choices misstate the counts.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Information and Ideas

items.stem: Engineers tested a bridge coating by exposing coated and uncoated steel panels to salt spray. The coated panels showed no rust after 500 hours, while the uncoated panels rusted within 50 hours. Which choice best states the main idea?
options: The study lasted only 50 hours in total.
The coating helped steel resist rust far longer than bare steel did.
Salt spray has no measurable effect on steel.
Uncoated steel resists rust better than coated steel.
items.explanation: The coated panels resisted rust for 500 hours versus 50 for the uncoated ones, so the coating greatly improved resistance; the others contradict the data.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Information and Ideas

items.stem: A survey found that 60 percent of commuters in a city use public transit and that 25 percent drive alone. Which choice states a fact supported by the text?
options: Use of public transit has been declining.
Twenty-five percent of commuters use public transit.
All commuters in the city drive alone.
items.explanation: A 60 percent share is a majority, so most commuters use public transit; the other choices are unsupported or reverse the figures.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Information and Ideas

items.stem: A store raised the price of a snack from $2 to $3, and weekly sales dropped from 500 units to 200 units. Which inference is best supported?
options: The snack became more popular after the change.
The store sold more units after the price rose.
The price change had no effect on weekly sales.
Customers were sensitive to the price increase.
items.explanation: Sales fell sharply when the price rose, which supports the idea that demand was sensitive to price; the other choices contradict the data.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Information and Ideas

items.stem: An author argues that a new reading program improves comprehension. Which evidence would best support the argument?
options: Students in the program scored higher on a comprehension test than a similar group not in the program.
The program meets on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
The program uses colorful posters and handouts.
The author personally enjoys reading the program materials.
items.explanation: A controlled comparison showing higher comprehension scores directly supports the argument; meeting days, posters, and personal preference are irrelevant.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Information and Ideas

items.stem: Corals obtain much of their energy from algae living in their tissues. When water grows too warm, the corals expel the algae and turn white. Which choice best states the main idea?
options: Corals are unaffected by changes in water temperature.
Warm water can cause corals to lose the algae they depend on.
Corals produce all of their own food without help.
The algae directly cause coral bleaching by overheating.
items.explanation: The text explains that warm water makes corals expel the algae they rely on; the other choices distort or contradict this relationship.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Information and Ideas

items.stem: A town built a new bridge, and within a year the number of shops on the formerly quiet east side doubled. Which inference is best supported?
options: The bridge is too narrow for most vehicles to use.
Fewer people visited the east side after the bridge opened.
The bridge likely made the east side easier to reach and drew commerce there.
The shops moved to the east side from the west side.
items.explanation: More shops appeared after the bridge opened, suggesting improved access drew commerce; the other choices are not supported by the text.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Information and Ideas

items.stem: The text states that a certain antibiotic stops bacteria from building cell walls. According to the text, how does the antibiotic act?
options: It speeds up the growth of bacteria.
It attacks healthy human cells directly.
It supplies bacteria with extra nutrients.
It prevents bacteria from forming cell walls.
items.explanation: The text says the antibiotic blocks cell-wall construction; it does not speed growth, harm human cells, or feed bacteria.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Information and Ideas

items.stem: A report notes that a country's forest cover rose from 30 percent in 1990 to 45 percent in 2020. Which choice best describes the trend?
options: Forest cover increased over the period.
Forest cover fell by about half over the period.
Forest cover stayed constant over the period.
items.explanation: Forest cover rose from 30 to 45 percent, which is an increase; the other choices misreport or reverse the trend.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Information and Ideas

items.stem: A plant kept in a dark closet grew tall and pale, while an identical plant near a sunny window stayed compact and green. Which inference is best supported?
options: The two plants belong to different species.
Light affects how the plant grows.
The closet plant received more light than the window plant.
The window plant was watered far more often.
items.explanation: The only difference described is light, so light likely shaped the plants' growth; the other choices contradict the scenario.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Information and Ideas

items.stem: Although the results were initially dismissed as anomalies, later studies showed the pattern was consistent and could not be ignored. As used in the text, the term anomalies most nearly means
options: simple arithmetic mistakes in the data
irregularities that seemed to break the expected pattern
deliberate frauds committed by the researchers
items.explanation: Anomalies are results that seem to break the expected pattern; the context is about odd results later shown to be real, not frauds or laws.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Craft and Structure

items.stem: The scientist was praised for her candid report, which acknowledged the study's limits rather than hiding them. As used in the text, the term candid most nearly means
items.explanation: Candid means frank and open, matching a report that admits limits; the other choices describe different qualities.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Craft and Structure

items.stem: Neither explanation rules out the other, so the two may both be partly true. As used in the text, the term mutually exclusive most nearly means
options: unable to be true at the same time
items.explanation: Mutually exclusive means the two cannot both be true at once, yet the sentence says both may be partly true, the opposite of that.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Craft and Structure

items.stem: Faced with conflicting data, the committee chose to postpone its decision rather than act hastily. As used in the text, the term postpone most nearly means
items.explanation: To postpone is to delay until later; the sentence contrasts it with acting hastily, not with canceling or announcing.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Craft and Structure

items.stem: The new evidence undermined the earlier theory, forcing researchers to revise it substantially. As used in the text, the term undermined most nearly means
items.explanation: Undermined means weakened the support for, which is why the theory had to be revised; the others mean the opposite or are unrelated.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Craft and Structure

items.stem: A passage first describes a common belief that goldfish have three-second memories, then presents experiments showing that goldfish can remember tasks for months. Which choice best describes the structure of the passage?
options: It lists the steps of an experiment without drawing any conclusion.
It compares two unrelated species of fish.
It defends the common belief with new experimental data.
It introduces a belief and then presents evidence that challenges it.
items.explanation: The passage poses a belief and then gives experiments that undercut it, the introduce-then-challenge structure; the others misdescribe the text.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Craft and Structure

items.stem: An author recounts her first attempt at coding, describing the errors she made, to open an article about learning from mistakes. What is the main purpose of the opening?
options: To illustrate through personal experience the article's theme
To prove that she is a professional programmer
To list the programming languages she has used
To criticize beginners who make errors
items.explanation: The personal story serves to illustrate the article's theme about learning from mistakes; it is not proof of expertise or a list of languages.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Craft and Structure

items.stem: In a passage about volcanoes, a sentence notes that most magma never reaches the surface. The author most likely includes this detail to
options: argue that volcanoes are harmless to people
emphasize how rare eruptions are compared with the total volume of magma
describe a famous eruption in careful detail
items.explanation: Saying most magma never surfaces emphasizes how rare eruptions are relative to total magma; it does not teach measurement or argue volcanoes are harmless.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Craft and Structure

items.stem: Text 1 argues that early cities formed mainly near rivers because of trade. Text 2 argues that some early cities formed in dry highlands for defense. How would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Text 1?
options: By claiming that rivers did not exist in early times
By rejecting the study of early cities altogether
By noting that river locations were not the only reason early cities formed
By agreeing that every early city formed beside a river
items.explanation: Text 2 highlights a different cause, highland defense, so its author would stress that rivers were not the only reason; the others misread both texts.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Craft and Structure

items.stem: Text 1 claims that a diet high in fiber reduces the risk of heart disease. Text 2 reports that a large study found no such link. Which choice best describes the relationship between the texts?
options: Text 2 provides evidence that supports the claim in Text 1.
Both texts describe the results of the same study.
Text 2 ignores the topic of diet entirely.
Text 2 presents findings that conflict with the claim in Text 1.
items.explanation: Text 1 claims a benefit and Text 2 reports no link, so Text 2 conflicts with Text 1; the other choices misstate their relationship.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Craft and Structure

items.stem: The committee's decision was met with ambivalence, since some members cheered while others objected. As used in the text, the term ambivalence most nearly means
items.explanation: Ambivalence means mixed or conflicting feelings, matching members who cheered and objected; the other choices imply a single uniform reaction.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Craft and Structure

items.stem: A passage begins with a question about why birds migrate, then surveys several competing hypotheses before noting that none fully explains the behavior. Which choice best describes the structure of the passage?
options: It focuses on the behavior of a single bird species.
It poses a question and reviews possible answers without settling it.
It answers the question definitively in the first sentence.
It ignores scientific explanations of migration.
items.explanation: The passage raises a question and surveys hypotheses without settling it; the other choices misdescribe the structure.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Craft and Structure

items.stem: The researcher was meticulous, checking every measurement twice before recording it. As used in the text, the term meticulous most nearly means
items.explanation: Meticulous means extremely careful and precise, matching the double-checking of measurements; the other choices are opposites or unrelated.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Craft and Structure

items.stem: An author describes a failed experiment in detail before describing the successful one that followed. The author most likely does this to
options: hide the successful result from readers
list the equipment used in the laboratory
show how the failure informed the later success
items.explanation: Describing the failure first shows how it informed the later success; the purpose is not to discourage, hide, or list equipment.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Craft and Structure

items.stem: Text 1 states that remote work increases productivity. Text 2 states that remote work weakens team creativity. Which choice best describes the relationship between the texts?
options: They consider different outcomes of the same practice.
They directly contradict each other about productivity.
They describe the results of identical studies.
They agree that remote work should be ended.
items.explanation: The texts examine different effects of remote work, productivity versus creativity, so they address different outcomes rather than contradicting.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Craft and Structure

items.stem: The first prototype was slow and unreliable. ______, the engineers redesigned it, and the second version performed well. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The redesign followed from the prototype's poor performance, so Therefore shows the logical result; the other transitions signal contrast or example.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Expression of Ideas

items.stem: The region receives very little rain. ______, farmers there have developed efficient irrigation methods. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Efficient irrigation is a result of scarce rain, so Consequently is the logical transition; the others signal similarity or addition.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Expression of Ideas

items.stem: Many people assume that bats are blind. ______, most bats can see quite well and rely on echolocation mainly in darkness. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence corrects the first assumption, so However signals the contrast; the others signal cause or addition.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Expression of Ideas

items.stem: The new battery stores more energy than older designs. ______, it can be charged far more quickly. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Quick charging is an additional benefit, so In addition fits; In contrast, Instead, and Therefore do not express an added point.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Expression of Ideas

items.stem: The experiment was run during a storm, with limited equipment, and still produced clear results. A student wants to emphasize that it succeeded despite the difficult conditions. Which choice most effectively uses the information to accomplish this goal?
options: The experiment produced results of some kind.
Even during a storm and with limited equipment, the experiment produced clear results.
The experiment used limited equipment throughout.
A storm occurred at some point during the experiment.
items.explanation: The goal is to stress success despite hard conditions, so the choice naming the storm and limited equipment while reporting clear results best fits.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Expression of Ideas

items.stem: A study found that participants who drank coffee slept less than participants who did not. A writer wants to introduce the study's main finding. Which choice best accomplishes this goal?
options: Coffee contains a stimulant called caffeine.
Adequate sleep is important for good health.
The study found that participants who drank coffee slept less than those who did not.
The study surveyed many people about their daily habits.
items.explanation: The goal is to state the main finding, so the sentence naming the sleep difference best accomplishes it; the others give background.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Expression of Ideas

items.stem: City A has a population of 1.2 million people, and City B has a population of 0.4 million. A writer wants to compare the populations of the two cities. Which choice best accomplishes this goal?
options: City A and City B are both cities.
City B has fewer parks than City A.
City A has a population of 1.2 million people.
City A has three times the population of City B.
items.explanation: The goal is comparison, and 1.2 million is three times 0.4 million, so the ratio statement is the only comparison; the others do not compare the cities.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Expression of Ideas

items.stem: The medicine relieved the symptoms within an hour. ______, it did not cure the underlying infection. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Relief and cure contrast, so However is correct; the others indicate cause, similarity, or result.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Expression of Ideas

items.stem: The company reduced waste by recycling. ______, it cut costs and improved its public image. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Cutting costs and improving the company's image followed from reducing waste, so As a result fits; the others signal contrast or example.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Expression of Ideas

items.stem: A drought lowered rainfall, and a nearby city diverted water from the lake. A writer wants to explain why the lake shrank. Which choice most effectively explains the cause?
options: The city is located near the lake.
Droughts occur in many regions around the world.
The lake shrank because both a drought and a city's water diversion reduced its supply.
The lake is smaller than several nearby lakes.
items.explanation: The goal is to explain the cause, so the sentence naming both the drought and the diversion best does this; the others are unrelated facts.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Expression of Ideas

items.stem: The team's first attempt failed to reach the summit. ______, they tried a different route the next day and succeeded. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Trying a different route after a failure shows persistence, so Nevertheless fits; Consequently, Similarly, and In conclusion do not.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Expression of Ideas

items.stem: The storm knocked out power to the neighborhood ______ residents used candles and flashlights until morning. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by a comma and and is correct; a comma alone creates a splice, and the other combinations are ungrammatical.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Standard English Conventions

items.stem: The biologist collected samples for three weeks ______ she analyzed them at the university laboratory. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: A semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses; a comma alone is a splice, a colon needs an explanation, and and alone is a run-on.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Standard English Conventions

items.stem: The recipe calls for three ingredients ______ flour, water, and salt. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: A colon introduces the list of ingredients; a comma or semicolon cannot introduce the list here, and and leaves the sentence ungrammatical.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Standard English Conventions

items.stem: The collection of rare coins ______ displayed in the museum's main hall. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is collection, which is singular, so is agrees; are, were, and have been are plural and disagree.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Standard English Conventions

items.stem: Neither the students nor the teacher ______ aware of the schedule change. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: With neither and nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject teacher, which is singular, so was is correct; the plural forms disagree.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Standard English Conventions

items.stem: The puppy wagged ______ tail happily when its owner came home. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The antecedent puppy is singular, so its is correct; it's means it is, and their and there do not agree with the antecedent or fit the sentence.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Standard English Conventions

items.stem: By the time the crew arrived, the fire ______ most of the old barn. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The destruction happened before the crew arrived, so the past perfect had destroyed is correct; the other tenses misplace the events in time.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Standard English Conventions

items.stem: Walking through the forest, ______. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: a family of deer was spotted near the stream
the stream was crossed by a family of deer
there were deer everywhere in the forest
we spotted a family of deer near the stream
items.explanation: The opening phrase describes the person or people walking, so we must be the subject; the other choices create a dangling modifier.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Standard English Conventions

items.stem: Covered in dust after the storm, ______. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the car needed a thorough wash
washing the car was clearly necessary
the storm left the car covered in dust
a wash was needed by the vehicle
items.explanation: The car is what was covered in dust, so the car must be the subject; the other choices attach the modifier to the wrong thing.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Standard English Conventions

items.stem: The new employee was praised for her punctuality, her accuracy, and ______. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: she was willing to help teammates
items.explanation: The list items must be parallel, so her willingness to help matches her punctuality and her accuracy; the others break the parallel structure.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Standard English Conventions

items.stem: The ______ decision to expand the program surprised the community. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English, given that the decision was made by the board?
items.explanation: The decision belongs to the board, so the singular possessive board's is correct; boards is plural, boards' is the plural possessive, and board lacks the possessive.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Standard English Conventions

items.stem: The scientists published ______ findings in a peer-reviewed journal. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: Scientists is plural, so the plural possessive their agrees; its is singular, it's means it is, and there is not possessive.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Standard English Conventions

items.stem: Although the trail was steep ______ the hikers reached the summit before noon. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: A dependent clause before an independent clause takes a comma, so the comma is correct; the semicolon and colon are wrong, and and is unnecessary.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Standard English Conventions

items.stem: The box of antique photographs ______ stored in the attic for many years. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: The subject is box, which is singular, so is agrees; the plural verbs are, were, and have been disagree with the subject.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Standard English Conventions

items.stem: If 3x + 5 = 20, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Subtract 5 from both sides to get 3x = 15, then divide by 3 to get x = 5; the other values do not satisfy the equation.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Algebra

items.stem: If 2(x - 3) = 10, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Divide both sides by 2 to get x - 3 = 5, then add 3 to get x = 8; the other choices misapply the operations.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Algebra

items.stem: A line passes through the points (1, 2) and (3, 8). What is the slope of the line?
items.explanation: Slope equals rise over run, (8 - 2) divided by (3 - 1) = 6/2 = 3; the other values invert or misread the differences.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Algebra

items.stem: The equation of a line is y = -2x + 7. What is the y-intercept of the line?
items.explanation: In slope-intercept form y = mx + b, b is the y-intercept, so it is 7; -2 is the slope and the other values are incorrect.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Algebra

items.stem: If x + y = 10 and x - y = 4, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Adding the equations eliminates y and gives 2x = 14, so x = 7; the other choices come from subtracting or misreading the system.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Algebra

items.stem: If 2x + y = 11 and y = 3, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Substitute y = 3 to get 2x + 3 = 11, so 2x = 8 and x = 4; the other values do not satisfy the equation.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Algebra

items.stem: The function f is defined by f(x) = 4x - 1. What is the value of f(3)?
items.explanation: Substitute 3 for x to get f(3) = 4(3) - 1 = 11; the other choices misapply the operation.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Algebra

items.stem: If g(x) = x squared plus 2x, what is the value of g(4)?
items.explanation: Compute g(4) = 4 squared plus 2(4) = 16 + 8 = 24; the other values come from squaring or adding incorrectly.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Algebra

items.stem: A taxi charges a flat fee of $3 plus $2 per mile. Which equation gives the total cost C, in dollars, for a ride of m miles?
items.explanation: The flat fee 3 is added to 2 dollars per mile times m, giving C = 3 + 2m; the others swap or misplace the terms.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Algebra

items.stem: If 5x - 4 > 11, which of the following is a possible value of x?
items.explanation: Adding 4 gives 5x > 15, so x > 3, and 4 is the only listed value greater than 3; the others are too small.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Algebra

items.stem: A gym charges a one-time fee of $50 plus $20 per month. After how many months will the total cost be $250?
items.explanation: Solve 50 + 20m = 250 to get 20m = 200, so m = 10 months; the other values do not satisfy the equation.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Algebra

items.stem: What is the solution set of the equation where the absolute value of x minus 3 equals 5?
items.explanation: The absolute value equals 5 when x - 3 = 5 or x - 3 = -5, giving x = 8 or x = -2; the other choices omit a case.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Algebra

items.stem: Line k has a slope of 1/2. What is the slope of a line that is perpendicular to line k?
items.explanation: A perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal of 1/2, which is -2; 2 is the reciprocal without the sign, and the others repeat the given fraction.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Algebra

items.stem: The equation y = 15x + 200 models the total cost y, in dollars, of producing x units. What does the number 200 represent?
options: The cost to produce each unit
The total number of units produced
The fixed cost when no units are produced
items.explanation: The constant 200 is the value of y when x = 0, so it is the fixed cost with no units produced; 15 is the per-unit cost.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Algebra

items.stem: Which value of b makes the system y = 3x + 2 and y = bx + 5 have no solution?
items.explanation: No solution requires equal slopes and different intercepts, so b = 3; the other values either intersect or make the equations coincide.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Algebra

items.stem: What are the solutions to the equation x squared minus 5x plus 6 equals 0?
items.explanation: Factor as (x - 2)(x - 3) = 0, so x = 2 or x = 3; the other pairs do not multiply to 6 and add to -5.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Advanced Math

items.stem: The function f(x) = x squared minus 4x plus 1 has its vertex at which point?
items.explanation: The vertex x-coordinate is negative b over 2a = 4/2 = 2, and f(2) = 4 - 8 + 1 = -3, so the vertex is (2, -3); the others are not the turning point.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Advanced Math

items.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (x + 3)(x - 3)?
items.explanation: This is a difference of squares, (x + 3)(x - 3) = x squared minus 9; the others add the square or misstate the cross terms.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Advanced Math

items.stem: Which expression is equivalent to 2x(3x - 4) + 8?
items.explanation: Distribute 2x to get 6x squared minus 8x, then add 8 for 6x squared minus 8x plus 8; the others drop or misplace terms.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Advanced Math

items.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (2 times x cubed)(5 times x to the fourth)?
items.explanation: Multiply coefficients 2 and 5 for 10, and add exponents 3 and 4 for x to the seventh, giving 10 times x to the seventh; the others add coefficients or multiply exponents.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Advanced Math

items.stem: Which expression is equivalent to x to the eighth divided by x squared, for x not equal to zero?
items.explanation: When dividing like bases, subtract exponents: 8 - 2 = 6, giving x to the sixth; the others add or multiply the exponents.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Advanced Math

items.stem: A population of bacteria doubles every hour. If it starts with 500 bacteria, which expression gives the population after h hours?
items.explanation: Doubling each hour multiplies the population by 2 each hour, so after h hours it is 500 times 2 to the h; the others add or misuse the exponent.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Advanced Math

items.stem: A car's value decreases by 15 percent each year. If its initial value is $20,000, which expression gives its value after t years?
items.explanation: A 15 percent yearly decrease leaves 85 percent each year, so the value is 20000 times 0.85 to the t; the others use the wrong base or linear decay.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Advanced Math

items.stem: How many real solutions does the equation x squared plus 4x plus 5 equals 0 have?
items.explanation: The discriminant is 4 squared minus 4(1)(5) = -4, which is negative, so there are no real solutions; the others miscount the roots.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Advanced Math

items.stem: If x squared equals 49 and x is greater than 0, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Taking the positive square root of 49 gives x = 7; -7 satisfies x squared = 49 but not the condition x > 0, and the others are not square roots.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Advanced Math

items.stem: If 1 over x equals 4, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: If 1 over x equals 4, multiply both sides by x and divide by 4 to get x = 1/4; the other values do not satisfy the equation.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Advanced Math

items.stem: If the square root of x equals 6, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Squaring both sides of the square root of x equals 6 gives x = 36; the other choices halve, divide, or misread the operation.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Advanced Math

items.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (x squared minus 4) divided by (x - 2), for x not equal to 2?
items.explanation: Factor the numerator as (x - 2)(x + 2); cancelling x - 2 leaves x + 2; the others come from incomplete factoring.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Advanced Math

items.stem: The function f(x) = (x - 1)(x + 5) has zeros at which values of x?
items.explanation: A product is zero when a factor is zero, so x - 1 = 0 or x + 5 = 0, giving x = 1 or x = -5; the other pairs have the wrong signs.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Advanced Math

items.stem: If 2 to the x equals 32, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Since 2 to the fifth = 32, x = 5; the other values give powers of 2 that are too small or too large.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Advanced Math

items.stem: A jacket originally costs $80 and is on sale for 25 percent off. What is the sale price?
items.explanation: A 25 percent discount removes 0.25 times 80 = $20, so the price is 80 - 20 = $60; $20 is the discount itself and the others are incorrect.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Problem-Solving and Data Analysis

items.stem: A recipe uses flour and sugar in a ratio of 3 to 1. If a baker uses 12 cups of flour, how many cups of sugar are needed?
items.explanation: The ratio 3 to 1 means sugar is one third of the flour, so 12 divided by 3 is 4 cups; the others invert or misapply the ratio.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Problem-Solving and Data Analysis

items.stem: A car travels 180 miles in 3 hours at a constant speed. What is its speed in miles per hour?
items.explanation: Speed equals distance divided by time, 180 divided by 3 = 60 miles per hour; the others multiply or misread the numbers.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Problem-Solving and Data Analysis

items.stem: A bag contains 4 red marbles and 6 blue marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the probability that it is red?
items.explanation: There are 4 red of 10 total marbles, so the probability is 4/10 = 2/5; 3/5 is the probability of blue and the others misstate the ratio.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Problem-Solving and Data Analysis

items.stem: What is the mean of the numbers 4, 8, 6, 10, and 12?
items.explanation: Sum the values to get 40, then divide by 5 to get a mean of 8; 10 is not the mean and 40 is the sum of the values.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Problem-Solving and Data Analysis

items.stem: In a survey, 40 of 200 respondents said they bike to work. What percent of respondents bike to work?
items.explanation: Divide the part by the whole, 40/200 = 0.20, or 20 percent; the others misplace the decimal or read the wrong number.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Problem-Solving and Data Analysis

items.stem: What is the median of the data set 3, 7, 9, 15, 20?
items.explanation: With five ordered values, the median is the middle one, 9; 7 and 15 flank it, and 10.8 is the mean rather than the median.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Problem-Solving and Data Analysis

items.stem: A rectangle has a length of 8 and a width of 5. What is its area?
items.explanation: Area of a rectangle is length times width, 8 times 5 = 40; 26 is the perimeter and the other values are incorrect.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: A circle has a radius of 3. What is its area, in terms of pi?
items.explanation: Area of a circle is pi times r squared, so pi times 9 = 9 pi; 6 pi is the circumference and the others omit pi or the square.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: A right triangle has legs of length 6 and 8. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
items.explanation: By the Pythagorean theorem, 6 squared + 8 squared = 36 + 64 = 100, so the hypotenuse is 10; 14 adds the legs and 48 is their product.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: In a 45-45-90 right triangle, each leg has length 5. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
items.explanation: In a 45-45-90 triangle the hypotenuse is a leg times the square root of 2, so it is 5 times the square root of 2; the square root of 3 fits a 30-60-90.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: A cube has an edge length of 4. What is its volume?
items.explanation: Volume of a cube is the edge cubed, 4 cubed = 64; 16 is the area of one face and the other values are incorrect.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: In a right triangle, the side opposite angle A is 3 and the hypotenuse is 5. What is the value of sin(A)?
items.explanation: Sine is opposite over hypotenuse, so sin(A) = 3/5; 4/5 is the cosine, and the other choices invert the ratio.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Geometry and Trigonometry

items.stem: A circle has a diameter of 10. What is its circumference, in terms of pi?
items.explanation: Circumference is pi times the diameter, so it is 10 pi; 5 pi uses the radius and the other values are incorrect.
items.reference: College Board Digital SAT suite - Math: Geometry and Trigonometry
